Let's solve this using the general formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (\frac{1}{1+2x}+\frac{1}{1-2x})\,\text{d}x & =\int \frac{1}{1+2x}\,\text{d}x+\int \frac{1}{1-2x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|1+2x|-\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|1-2x|+C \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡|\frac{1+2x}{1-2x}|+\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡K \\  & =\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{ln}⁡(K|\frac{1+2x}{1-2x}|)\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that we used the laws of logarithms to write the result as a single logarithm.
